summary: NASA's 3D model of the Saturn V, cut into its stages where the model's width steps, staging in the order of Apollo 11's flight, much faster than real.

claims.claim: The pieces separate in the order of a real flight: the S-IC, the interstage ring, the launch escape tower, the S-II, then the spacecraft leaves the S-IVB.
claims.how: The drive moves each piece at its time on a 12-second clock; the test checks the order.

sources.title: Saturn V
sources.says: First stage separation occurred less than one second after the engines were cut off ... At about T+3 minutes 12 seconds, the interstage ring dropped ... Shortly after interstage separation, the Launch Escape System was also jettisoned ... At about T+9 minutes 8 seconds ... separating the S-II ... About 40 minutes after TLI, the Apollo Command and Service module (CSM) separated from the third stage.

claims.claim: The S-IC is the bottom 38% of the rocket's height (42 m of 110.6 m).
claims.how: The pieces are cut at shares of the model's height where its width steps, checked against the stages' lengths.

sources.title: Saturn V
sources.says: Height 110.6 m (363 ft); S-IC length 42 m (138 ft); S-IVB 58 ft 7 in (17.86 m) tall.

claims.note: The cuts follow the model, which is an artist's model rather than an engineering drawing.

simplified: Staging that took hours is shown in 12 seconds.
The flames are glowing cones, not a simulation of the exhaust.
The model paints a band of the first stage navy blue; the real stage was white there, so it is drawn white.
The panels round the lunar module and the lunar module itself are not shown separately.
